text:
james_acme: Hey team, after our tenant migration some of our calls to the service endpoint are getting TLS errors and some resolve to a public IP. Not sure if split-horizon issue. Can someone help?
michelle_support: sorry to hear that — can you share a dig/nslookup from the app VPC?
james_acme: digging now, here's dig from a pod node (via kubectl exec):
```
$ dig +short service.prod.acme.internal @169.254.169.253
52.44.12.9
```
james_acme: That 52.44.12.9 is a public ELB IP — shouldn't be reachable from the VPC. We get TLS SNI mismatch on client side.
ian_sre: interesting — sounds like the private hosted zone isn't being used. Two quick checks: 1) confirm VPC association with the private hosted zone; 2) check node-local DNS / nodelocaldns cache.
raj_neteng: also check if there's a forwarding resolver rule that points to a third-party resolver. If UDP53 blocked, sometimes TCP fallback to public resolver happens.
michelle_support: @james_acme can you run: `dig +trace service.prod.acme.internal` and `kubectl exec -n app nslookup service.prod.acme.internal` and paste outputs?
james_acme: pasted short outputs:
```
$ dig +trace service.prod.acme.internal
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> +trace service.prod.acme.internal
...
;; Received 1 answers, 1 authority, 0 additional
service.prod.acme.internal. 60 IN A 52.44.12.9
```
```
$ kubectl exec -it pod-123 -- nslookup service.prod.acme.internal
Server: 169.254.169.253
Address: 169.254.169.253#53
Name: service.prod.acme.internal
Address: 52.44.12.9
```
james_acme: our expected private IP is 10.100.45.22.
alice_eng: do you have a private hosted zone for `prod.acme.internal` in your account? or could there be a private zone in a different account that's associated to this VPC?
james_acme: we used to have a private hosted zone in our tenant account but DB migration team said they created a new one in the platform account during cutover.
ian_sre: that lines up — likely two private hosted zones with same name in different accounts, one associated and one not, or a public record leaking. AWS Route53 will pick the hosted zone that is associated with your VPC; if the platform account zone isn't associated, queries will hit public resolution.
raj_neteng: can you list hosted zones associated with the VPC? from platform side: `aws route53domains list-hosted-zones-by-vpc --vpc-id vpc-0ab12cd34` or in console VPC -> Route53 associations.
james_acme: I don't have platform account access — can platform team check?
michelle_support: looping in platform infra: @ian_sre @raj_neteng — can you confirm if `prod.acme.internal` private hosted zone exists in platform account and whether the customer's VPC is associated?
ian_sre: I'm running a quick lookup from our side — giving me a second.
support-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1148 (private-dns-shadowing) — assigned to infra-routing.
ian_sre: confirmed: platform account has a private hosted zone `prod.acme.internal` but it is NOT associated to the customer's VPC. The customer's account still has an old hosted zone that is associated but missing the newer records. That mismatch explains the public answer.
ajames_acme: any immediate workaround? Traffic failing TLS.
raj_neteng: short-term: add the correct A record in the associated hosted zone to point to 10.100.45.22 OR associate the platform hosted zone to the VPC (preferred). Also ensure node-local cache TTL cleared.
alice_eng: steps: 1) platform infra can associate their private hosted zone to the customer's VPC (AWS console or `associate-vpc-with-hosted-zone`), 2) run `kubectl -n kube-system exec -it nodelocaldns -- kill -HUP 1` or restart nodelocaldns DaemonSet to flush cache, 3) verify with `dig @169.254.169.253 service.prod.acme.internal +short` returns 10.100.45.22.
james_acme: is there any risk associating zones across accounts? We were told that's sensitive.
ian_sre: it's a standard cross-account VPC association pattern but requires proper IAM control. If policy forbids, then platform can create a delegation/forwarding rule instead.
michelle_support: also check egress allowlist: if UDP53/53 to the resolver IP is blocked, pods may fallback in weird ways. Can you run `iptables -t nat -L` or show egress SG/NACL config?
james_acme: our egress SG allows outbound UDP/TCP 53 to 169.254.169.253.
raj_neteng: good. If for some reason node-local DNS tries public, that explains public IP. Once association fixed and caches flushed should be fine.
support-bot: Escalation note: add request to infra-runbook for cross-account hosted zone association and add a follow-up to clean up the old hosted zone in customer account to prevent confusion.
ian_sre: I'll make the association now and ping when complete.
ian_sre: association complete — platform hosted zone associated to vpc-0ab12cd34.
ian_sre: flushing node-local cache on affected nodes, restarting pods that had DNS cached.
ian_sre: can someone from ACME re-test?
james_acme: testing...
```
$ dig +short service.prod.acme.internal @169.254.169.253
10.100.45.22
```
james_acme: TLS error gone, calls succeed, thanks.
michelle_support: great — we should also schedule zone cleanup: remove old associated hosted zone in customer account or deprecate it to avoid future drift.
alice_eng: note for runbook: when migrating private zones between accounts, ensure: export zone file, associate target zone to all VPCs, flush caches, then remove old zone associations.
james_acme: appreciate the quick help — please keep INC-2026-1148 open until cleanup done. :heart:
michelle_support: will keep open and add postmortem checklist. :thumbsup:
ian_sre: closing the immediate incident, leaving action items for platform infra and product to follow up.
